figure: Intro Fig. 1; ch. 2 Figs 1, 6; App. B Figs 1, 6
period: Chalcolithic; Iron Age II (7th c. BCE); Roman (contemporary with Khirbet Qumran); medieval (c. 10th c. CE); 18th-19th c.
quote: L'entrée reconnue de 11Q s'ouvre au sud-est.
notes: Grid printed as the 'entrance point according to the Israeli Grid' (survey G. Levi, Mabat 3D, March 2017) (p.1 n.1); values are in the New Israel Grid range, not converted. Relations to features not keyed here: c.1.5 km N of Khirbet Qumran and 500 m N of Cave 1Q (p.1); de Vaux: almost 2 km N of the Khirbet, a little S of Cave 3Q (p.22); 3Q 300 m N of 11Q (p.71 n.2); Patrich's cave 24 50 m N (p.63). In the lowest ledge of the cliff, opening SE, about 20 m above (gentle slope) the path at the cliff foot 150 m away (p.46); Harding: some 50 feet up the scarp (p.23). Natural karst cavity in Turonian limestone (Bina fm.) formed by horizontal dissolution; ceiling a single slab tilted to the S; void 'about two metres' high (p.46, 67). length_m 19 = printed dimension '1900cm' on the section App. B Fig. 6 (p.76); the cave as drawn there reaches slightly beyond it. Plan_scaled values for comparison: App. B Fig. 1 (p.72; 1 m grid, scale bar, N arrow) c.21 m from the mouth to the inner (NW) end and c.16.5 m maximum width; Humbert Fig. 6 (p.50) bounding extent c.17.5 m S-N x 19.5 m W-E; Patrich plan (Fig. 12 p.24) c.19 m. One recognised entrance (SE); a hypothesised second entrance (shaft crevice above the back h) could not have been a passage (p.52). Entrance blocked when found in 1956. One natural pillar divides it into two chambers (p.67); Humbert distinguishes rooms b, c, d and other parts a-x (Fig. 6).

quote: The doorway, once cleared, is 1.60 meters wide, 1.35 meters high
notes: Size after de Vaux cleared and widened it, height measured to the 'Roman floor' (field notes 1 March 1956, French p.16, English p.19; repeated p.52, 59, 78). Humbert: not the primitive opening; ancient access narrower and lower (p.48, 52), perhaps a very low crawl hole sealed by two stones (p.61-62). Opens on vertical fracture N150 (geology p.67). Framed by two rocks; only two men could stand between them (p.52). Present-day mouth gaping, c.6 m wide on App. B Fig. 1 (p.72, plan_scaled).

quote: Elle comprend une première chambre circulaire
notes: De Vaux: first, circular chamber (p.22); front part of the cavity open onto the slope (p.48); standing-height zone on Fig. 6, but the authors of the cache could barely stand there (p.51). Plan_scaled on Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m, N arrow): c.8 m W-E x 6.5 m S-N. Fill: yellow water-laid layer c.50 cm; 54 cm between Chalcolithic and Roman levels (p.18-19). Called 'entrance chamber'/'entrance hall' in App. B (Operation B on its W side, p.78).

quote: Il fallait alors se courber sous le plafond bas en (l)
notes: Passage between b and c where a large portion of the ceiling collapsed in geological times; low ceiling, floor rising from b to c (p.51). Humbert reconstructs a dry-stone partition v-w across it, pierced by a door (p.64). Dims = lowered-vault zone on Fig. 6, low precision.

quote: une grande chambre dont le sol rocheux monte rapidement
notes: De Vaux: large chamber behind the first, rock floor rising rapidly (p.22); extends to the right of b (p.48); larger than b but standing area reduced by the rising floor and the raised bench j (p.51). Back (eastern limit) at h, a talus of loose earth (p.52). Plan_scaled Fig. 6: c.8.5 m S-N (l to h) x 6.5 m W-E (standing area; bench j extends further). Probably the 'chambre du fond' of the geology appendix (p.70 Fig. 7), not equated by the source.

quote: nous considérons cette dernière comme la seconde chambre de la grotte intérieure
notes: Opens to the left from c and from b; easier from b (floor descends from b to d), awkward from c via a ledge ('ressaut'); one can stand in it (p.48, 51). Small ('exiguë'), floor now covered with boulders moved from f; lower than c, flat ceiling shared with c (p.51). Dims plan_scaled on Fig. 6 (standing zone incl. block q).

quote: Dans une fracture du banc supérieur ... qui rejoint le diverticule (e)
notes: Side recess on the E side of b, crossed by section D-E (Fig. 6). A fracture of the upper rock bed, seen on the façade at top right of the entrance, joins it; strong water infiltration (p.57).

quote: On arrête le travail dans la galerie, qui s'enfonce à gauche
notes: De Vaux's 'gallery to the left': dead-end corridor narrowing (f-g), very low ceiling, along the south side; full of large stones; passage d-f narrow and lowered; work stopped 13 March 1956 as dangerous (p.17-18, 48, 51, 57).

quote: pour observer l'élargissement (g), dans lequel on hésite à s'engager tant il est bas
notes: Widening at the end of gallery f; very low (p.51).

quote: la limite orientale n'est ici qu'un talus de terre meuble
notes: Back/eastern limit of c, where the rock ceiling ends in an overhang; a shaft-like crevice in the cliff above roughly corresponds to it (see 11Q.crevasse). No size keyed.

quote: la banquette (j) surélevée en équerre, large et impropre à la déambulation
notes: Raised, wide, L-shaped bench in c (p.51); drawn on Fig. 6 as a lowered-vault zone along the N side of c running to the gallery end g. Dims = whole j zone on Fig. 6, low precision.

quote: un reste de maçonnerie dans l'anfractuosité (k) : le creux du rocher va en s'amincissant
notes: Narrowing rock cleft holding masonry remnant u (p.64).

quote: encombrée d'un gros quartier (q) détaché du plafond avant l'époque historique
notes: Large block fallen from the ceiling before historical times, deeply sunk in the rubble (p.51).

figure: ch. 2 Fig. 6 (p. 50); geology Fig. 7 (p.70); App. B Fig. 1 'X' (p.72), Fig. 17 (p.83)
quote: La cavité est séparée en deux chambres par un pilier naturel
notes: Geological remnant in the form of a pillar around which the cavity is organised (p.51); untouched by karstification; separates entrance chamber from back chamber (p.67, Fig. 7 p.70); 2017: central rock joining ceiling and ground, not aligned with the 'arch' axis (p.82). Plan_scaled: Fig. 6 c.2 x 2 m; App. B Fig. 1 ('X') c.2 x 2.5 m.

quote: D'après les photographies, nous restituons trois éléments construits (u), (v), (w)
notes: Masonry remnant hooked in cleft k; would have tied partition u-v to the south wall, closing d up to pillar r (p.64). Restored from 1956 photographs; dry stone ('pierres sèches'), same build and date as the other built elements; demolished by later diggers, not seen in place by Patrich (p.57, 63-64). Humbert attributes them to the Chalcolithic; App. B (p.82-85) suggests such structures were safety walls built in 1956.

quote: érigée avec soin, sans assises, les blocs imbriqués les uns dans les autres
notes: Against the natural pillar r; best preserved; no courses, interlocking blocks, held by leaning on the rock; did not support the vault; rested on rock, not below the 'Roman floor' level (p.64). With w part of partition v-w between b and c, which 'la porte perçait' (p.64). Probably = App. B 'thick dry-stone wall along the axis of the pillar' (Fig. 19 B), not equated by the source. Restored from 1956 photographs; dry stone ('pierres sèches'), same build and date as the other built elements; demolished by later diggers, not seen in place by Patrich (p.57, 63-64). Humbert attributes them to the Chalcolithic; App. B (p.82-85) suggests such structures were safety walls built in 1956.

quote: une photographie montre le bloc ... surmonté d'une maçonnerie (w) de plusieurs pierres
notes: Masonry of several stones on a large rock standing like a door jamb at the 'entrance of the inner room'; continued the partition isolating b from c (p.64); now dismantled (p.55). Restored from 1956 photographs; dry stone ('pierres sèches'), same build and date as the other built elements; demolished by later diggers, not seen in place by Patrich (p.57, 63-64). Humbert attributes them to the Chalcolithic; App. B (p.82-85) suggests such structures were safety walls built in 1956.

quote: Un parement de pierre plus profond (x), visible sur les photographies
notes: Lower built stone facing on the left side where the gallery starts, south of b towards d; rectifies the south wall of d; attests a lower floor (p.51, 64). Restored from 1956 photographs; dry stone ('pierres sèches'), same build and date as the other built elements; demolished by later diggers, not seen in place by Patrich (p.57, 63-64). Humbert attributes them to the Chalcolithic; App. B (p.82-85) suggests such structures were safety walls built in 1956.

period: Humbert: sealing of the cache (Qumran period); App. B: natural
quote: Il faut y voir la preuve que la grotte a été scellée de main d'homme
notes: Large collapsed blocks of rock/pudding stone covering the entrance in 1956 (diary 26 Feb 1956, p.18); Skehan: 'plugged at the opening with fairly enormous masses of rock' (p.24); Harding: entrance collapsed anciently leaving a very small hole (p.23). Humbert: man-made sealing, long pile of stones at the foot of the rock face, plus two stones wedged between vault and fill (p.52, 61-62). App. B: blockage explainable by natural processes, human contribution not excluded (p.73 and n.7).

quote: Un foyer, à la limite de l'abri pour éviter l'enfumage, atteste l'habitation chalcolithique
notes: Inferred from a stony ashy layer on bedrock; 'plausible à l'aplomb du porche' (p.59).

quote: une crevasse en puits et en contre-haut correspond grosso modo au fond (h)
notes: Shaft-like crevice in the cliff façade further north, in the horizontal fracture of the rock bed, above and roughly corresponding to the back (h); hypothesised second entrance; reconsidered March 2017, could not have been a passage; a contiguous space emptied by suffosion was accessible from the cave (cf. 11Q.upper) (p.52).

class_as_printed: crevice to the right of the entrance
quote: The crevice to the right of the entrance, cleared by us, was full
notes: Patrich 1988: full of sterile aeolian sand (p.24); App. B n.9 places it north-east of the entrance (p.78). Possibly = Humbert's e (not equated).

quote: or in the north crevice
notes: Named by Patrich (p.24); possibly the same as the 'innermost crevice'.

quote: two pieces of cloth were found in the innermost crevice
notes: Named by Patrich (p.24).

quote: La cavité s'ouvre sur une fracture verticale d'orientation N 150°
notes: Vertical fracture that determines the entrance; strike N 150° (fracture orientation, not an opening direction); conjugate at the ceiling with the N 30° fracture (p.67).

quote: conjuguée au plafond avec une fracture N 30°
notes: Ceiling fracture at the cave entrance, strike N 30° (p.67, Fig. 5). General fracturing N 30° and N 120° measured on a slab just north of the entrance (Fig. 2).

quote: Dans une fracture du banc supérieur (fig. 5), repérée en façade à droite au sommet
notes: Fracture of the upper rock bed seen on the façade at top right of the entrance, joining diverticule e; strong infiltration (p.57). May coincide with F150/F30 (not equated).

quote: terra rossa (c'est le cas du fond de la cavité, sur sa paroi nord)
notes: Karst conduit (natural solution channel) at the back of the cavity on its north wall, filled with terra rossa (p.67).

quote: soit d'éboulis consolidés comme à l'entrée de la grotte coté nord
notes: Karst conduit at the entrance, north side, partly filled with consolidated slope scree (p.67, Fig. 6).

quote: The area above the cave is naturally shaped as a catchment basin (impluvium)
notes: Overflow from the slope directly above the entrance; basin delimited from a DTM covers about 3000 m2 including 11Q (p.73).

quote: Block A to the west collapsed from the ceiling above the entrance
notes: Large conglomerate block in front of the entrance (W). Dims scaled on App. B Fig. 1 (p.72; 1 m grid, scale bar, N arrow). Possibly one of the 'deux rochers qui encadrent l'entrée' (p.52), not equated.

quote: the eastern block lying farther away (about 1 m) from the entrance
notes: Fell from the cliff side orthogonal to the entrance; lies about 1 m farther from the entrance (reading of '1 m' ambiguous, not keyed as rel_distance); redirects part of the run-off into the cave (p.73). Dims scaled on App. B Fig. 1 (p.72).

quote: a long, narrow breach runs from the ceiling to the bottom of the sediment
notes: Behind block A; fine sediment covered by a conglomerate slab accumulated between block A and the entrance (p.73).

quote: A fallen conglomerate slab is also visible to the right of entrance hall.
notes: Inside the entrance hall, on its right (p.82).

quote: forming a sort of “arch” spanning through the cave's width
notes: Rock layer partly detached from the ceiling in the middle of the cave between inner and outer parts, spanning the cave's width, seemingly sustained by the pillar (not aligned with it) (p.82). length = span of the stippled 'arch' band on Fig. 1 (p.72); band c.2.5-4 m wide.

quote: a remarkable wedge behind the “arch”, to the left of the “pillar”
notes: Rock wedge detaching along sub-vertical NW-SE faults (p.82).

quote: a thick dry-stone wall along the axis of the “pillar” (Fig. 19, B)
notes: Documented in 1956 photographs (Fig. 19, 3 March 1956; Fig. 20), never mentioned by de Vaux, dismantled before Patrich's 1988 work; left part of the pillar wall rebuilt during the 1956 excavation; suggested to be safety walls built by the 1956 excavators (p.82-85). Probably = Humbert's v (not equated by the source).

quote: more stone structures at the shoulders of the “arch” (Fig. 19, A,C)
notes: Structure A at a shoulder of the 'arch'. Documented in 1956 photographs (Fig. 19, 3 March 1956; Fig. 20), never mentioned by de Vaux, dismantled before Patrich's 1988 work; left part of the pillar wall rebuilt during the 1956 excavation; suggested to be safety walls built by the 1956 excavators (p.82-85). Probably among Humbert's u/w (not equated).

quote: more stone structures at the shoulders of the “arch” (Fig. 19, A,C)
notes: Structure C at a shoulder of the 'arch'. Documented in 1956 photographs (Fig. 19, 3 March 1956; Fig. 20), never mentioned by de Vaux, dismantled before Patrich's 1988 work; left part of the pillar wall rebuilt during the 1956 excavation; suggested to be safety walls built by the 1956 excavators (p.82-85). Probably among Humbert's u/w (not equated).

quote: the room, rectangular in plan (Fig. 1), measures about 2 × 6 m
notes: Found March 2017; entered by a narrow vertical passage (2.5 m) in the northern corner of the cave; height 3.5 m at the entry point, 1.2 m at the deep (North) end; W side limestone, other sides and ceiling conglomerate; no evidence of human activity (p.85). Opening is the vertical passage, so no compass direction keyed. On Fig. 1 (p.72) it lies on the NE side of the cave, c.7 m long (plan_scaled). Probably the space 'vidé par un phénomène de suffosion' of p.52.

quote: a narrow vertical passage, 2.5 m in length
notes: In the northern corner of the cave; found after removing fallen stones obstructing it (p.85). Length is vertical.
